description: Read and search an Obsidian vault. Provides hybrid search, tag queries, and a structured memory layer (About Me/) for personalization across conversations.
instructions:
Read and search an Obsidian vault. Use vault_search and vault_read_note to find and read notes. Use vault_get_memory to retrieve user preferences and context from About Me/ files.

Vault content is Obsidian Flavored Markdown. No tools that modify the vault are available.

tools.name: vault_find_orphans
tools.title: Find Orphans
tools.description:
Find notes with no incoming links from other notes or canvases — orphans are disconnected from the knowledge graph and may be forgotten or need linking. A note that only links to itself still counts as an orphan.

Example: vault_find_orphans({})
Example: vault_find_orphans({ exclude_folders: ["Templates", "Archive"], limit: 20 })

When to use: Vault maintenance — surfacing notes to integrate into the graph.
Prefer vault_get_backlinks to check the connectivity of one specific note rather than scanning the whole vault.

Parameters:
- exclude_folders replaces the defaults, it does not add to them — list a default yourself to keep it. Pass [] for no exclusions. Each entry names a whole folder, subfolders included ("Projects" also excludes "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/"), ignoring ASCII letter case. Excluded notes are left out of the results; links from them still count as incoming links. The defaults' daily notes folder is the one vault_get_daily_note's path starts with; when it is the vault root or blank, the defaults hold no daily folder.
- limit applies after exclusions and sorting by most recently modified. Nothing in the response signals truncation: exactly limit results may mean more exist, so raise limit to check.

Behavior: A file change takes a few seconds to appear here, so a link written moments ago may not count yet.

Errors:
- An empty array means no orphans were found (after exclusions), not an error.
- "too many excluded folders" — exclude_folders has more than 994 entries; pass a shorter list, then retry.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of note metadata (path, title, tags, related, folder (top-level folder), type, created (null when missing or not an ISO date), modified, bytes, leading_callout, additional_properties), sorted by most recently modified. The bytes field is the on-disk file size. A leading_callout field appears only when the note has one; additional_properties only when frontmatter has keys outside title, type, created, related, and tags.

exclude_folders.description: Folder paths to exclude (e.g. Projects; default: the daily notes folder, "Templates", "About Me")

tools.name: vault_get_backlinks
tools.title: Get Backlinks
tools.description:
Find all notes and canvases that link to a given note or canvas — captures [[wikilinks]], [markdown](links), ![[embeds]], wikilinks inside frontmatter properties (e.g. related:), and canvas cards that embed the file. Heading anchors ([[note#heading]]) and aliases ([[note|alias]]) resolve as backlinks to the base note. Links inside code blocks are ignored; a note linking to itself appears in its own backlinks.

Example: vault_get_backlinks({ path: "Projects/vault-cortex.md" })
Example: vault_get_backlinks({ path: "Diagrams/architecture.canvas" })

When to use: Understanding what references a note or canvas, assessing its connectivity before editing or deleting, or finding related notes via the graph.
For outgoing links (what a note links TO), use vault_get_outgoing_links. To find notes nothing else links to, use vault_find_orphans.

Parameters:
- path: pass the target's own path, never a link's text: a link written as [[Note]], as a relative ../Note.md, or as a full path counts toward the note it resolves to.

Returns: JSON with path (the queried note or canvas), backlinks (array of { path, title, bytes } sorted by title; title is a canvas source's file name without .canvas; bytes is the source's on-disk size), and count.

Errors:
- "path must end in …" — add the .md or .canvas extension
- A path nothing links to returns an empty result (count 0), not an error; links from a note written or changed in the last few seconds may not appear yet. If you expected links, find valid paths with vault_search or vault_list_notes.
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

path.description: Exact vault-relative path including .md or .canvas extension (e.g. "Projects/vault-cortex.md"). Case-sensitive.

tools.name: vault_get_daily_note
tools.title: Get Daily Note
tools.description:
Read a daily note by date, using the vault's configured Daily Notes folder and filename date format. Each setting comes from the DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER / DAILY_NOTES_FORMAT env vars, falling back to the vault's .obsidian/daily-notes.json, then to "Daily Notes" and YYYY-MM-DD.

Example: vault_get_daily_note({ date: "2026-05-13" })
Example: vault_get_daily_note({}) — returns today's daily note

When to use: When you need today's or a specific date's daily note. For recent vault activity, vault_recent_notes lists the most recently changed notes; it has no date filter.

Parameters:
- date: always YYYY-MM-DD, whatever filename format the vault uses; past and future dates are both valid.

Errors:
- "invalid date" — use YYYY-MM-DD format
- "… is not a calendar date" — the date has the YYYY-MM-DD form but names a day that doesn't exist, such as 2026-02-30; pass a real date
- "daily note format contains unsupported token(s): ..." — the configured format uses tokens the server cannot reproduce; the message names the tokens and the fix
- "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" / "absolute path blocked" — the configured daily notes folder or format leads outside the vault or into a hidden folder; change it in Obsidian, or set DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER and DAILY_NOTES_FORMAT
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …", "EACCES: …" or another filesystem error code — the message says what to do

Returns: JSON with path (string — resolved vault-relative path), content (string|null — the note's full text, properties block included, or null when the note doesn't exist), and exists (boolean).

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. "2026-05-13", "2025-12-31"). Defaults to today in the server's timezone.

tools.name: vault_get_memory
tools.title: Get Memory
tools.description:
Read semantic memory from About Me/ files. These are structured memory files containing dated bullet entries organized under H2 headings. With file: that file. With file+section: just that H2 section's entries. No args: every file, joined by --- lines — can be large.

With file+on_or_after: only the entries dated on or after that date (inclusive), in document order (newest first when new entries go at the top, their default position). Add section to scope to one H2 section; omit it to read every H2 section's entries in the file, each keeping its section attribution.

Example: vault_get_memory({ file: "Principles" }) — the whole file
Example: vault_get_memory({ file: "Principles", section: "Decision heuristics (newest first)" })
Example: vault_get_memory({ file: "Opinions", section: "Code patterns", on_or_after: "2026-09-01" })
Example: vault_get_memory({ file: "Opinions", on_or_after: "2026-09-01" }) — every section's entries since the date

When to use: Reading user preferences, principles, opinions, or other persistent context stored in About Me/ files. Call vault_list_memory_files first to discover valid file and section names.
Prefer vault_read_note for reading non-memory notes. To find entries by topic across every file, use vault_memory_recall.

Errors:
- "section requires a file" / "on_or_after requires a file" — add file
- "memory file not found" — call vault_list_memory_files to discover valid names
- "memory file must not start with a dot" / "memory file must be a bare name without path separators" / "memory file must be named without .md" — each message names the part of the name to drop
- "section not found: …" — no H2 heading matches; the message lists the file's sections
- "date must be a real ISO calendar date" — on_or_after must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date
- "cannot read memory file …" / "cannot list memory folder …" — a memory file, or the About Me/ folder itself on a call without file, can't be read: check file against vault_list_memory_files (a name longer than the filesystem allows fails here); otherwise ask the vault's owner to check the folder

Returns: Without on_or_after, raw markdown with the properties block stripped, or an empty string when no memory files exist yet. With on_or_after, JSON { entries, total, on_or_after } where each entry is { file, section, date, text } — text is the full raw entry markdown (bullet + continuation lines, wikilinks intact). An empty match returns { entries: [], total: 0, on_or_after }.

file.description: Memory file name without .md (e.g. "Principles", "Opinions"). Use the exact letter case.

section.description: H2 section heading (e.g. "Decision heuristics (newest first)"). Matched case-insensitively, with or without the "(newest first)" suffix. Omit to read the whole file.

tools.name: vault_get_outgoing_links
tools.title: Get Outgoing Links
tools.description:
Find all notes and files a given note or canvas links to. For notes: [[wikilinks]], [markdown](links), ![[embeds]], and wikilinks inside frontmatter properties (e.g. related:). For canvas files: file nodes (vault-relative paths embedded in the canvas), not links inside text cards. Links inside code blocks are ignored; self-links are included. Each target is listed once, however often the note links to it. A broken link's path is its target text up to any #heading or |alias, in its original letter case, with a markdown link's %-escapes decoded.

Example: vault_get_outgoing_links({ path: "Projects/vault-cortex.md" })
Example: vault_get_outgoing_links({ path: "Diagrams/architecture.canvas" })

When to use: Navigating the graph forward, auditing broken links in one note or canvas, or checking dependencies before editing.
For incoming links (what links TO a note), use vault_get_backlinks.

Parameters:
- path: a note or canvas created or moved in the last few seconds is not found yet.

Returns: JSON with path, outgoing_links (array of { path, title, exists, kind, bytes, daily_note_forward_ref } sorted by target path), and count. When exists is true: kind "note" is a markdown note readable via vault_read_note; kind "file" is a non-markdown file (.canvas, image, PDF). When exists is false the link is broken, and kind is "note" even for a path like "diagram.png". The title field is null for files and broken links. The daily_note_forward_ref flag is true on a broken link into the vault's daily notes folder — expected "create on click" navigation to a daily note that doesn't exist yet, not genuine breakage — and false otherwise, including when the daily notes folder is the vault root or blank. The bytes field is the on-disk size of a note or file (null for broken links).

Errors:
- "path must end in …" — add the .md or .canvas extension
- A path that does not exist, or one in a dot-prefixed folder, returns an empty result (count 0), not an error, just as a note with no outbound links does. If you expected links, find valid paths with vault_search or vault_list_notes.
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

path.description: Exact vault-relative path including .md or .canvas extension (e.g. "Projects/vault-cortex.md"). Case-sensitive.

tools.name: vault_list_memory_files
tools.title: List Memory Files
tools.description:
Discovery tool — lists About Me/ memory files with each file's heading outline, per-section entry counts, and leading callout. An entry is a dated bullet line ("- **YYYY-MM-DD**: text"). Does NOT return actual entries.

Example: vault_list_memory_files()

When to use: Discovering what memory files and sections exist — and what each file is for — BEFORE calling vault_get_memory; this tool gives the valid file and section names. To find entries by topic instead, use vault_memory_recall.

Behavior: Lists every .md file directly inside About Me/, sorted by file name, whether or not it has frontmatter or a scope callout. Subfolders are not read, and hidden (dot-prefixed) files and names ending in .md.md (such as Opinions.md.md) are skipped.

Errors:
- An empty or nonexistent memory folder returns an empty array, not an error.
- "cannot list memory folder …" — a file stands at the memory folder's path, or its permissions block the server; ask the vault's owner to fix it
- "cannot read memory file …" — one listed file can't be read, which fails the whole listing; retry once, then ask the vault's owner to check that file

Returns: JSON array of file outlines, each { file, title, bytes, entry_policy, leading_callout, headings } — file is the name the other memory tools take as file (no .md); title is the title property, or file when there is none; bytes is the on-disk file size; headings lists H1 and H2 headings in order, with entry_count on H2s; leading_callout is the top-of-file callout ({ type, title, body }; by convention a "Scope of this file" block describing what belongs in the file), or null; entry_policy is "append-only" (the default: by convention, entries are never edited or deleted) or "living" (a current-state file whose expired entries may be pruned; declared via `entry-policy` frontmatter). The server does not enforce either policy.

tools.name: vault_list_notes
tools.title: List Notes
tools.description:
List .md file paths in the vault, optionally filtered by folder and/or glob pattern. Returns paths only — not content or metadata.

Example: vault_list_notes({ folder: "Projects" })
Example: vault_list_notes({ glob: "**/*session-log*.md" })
Example: vault_list_notes({ folder: "Projects", glob: "*.md" }) — the folder's top-level notes only

When to use: Browsing what exists in a folder by filename, or finding notes matching a path pattern.
Prefer vault_search_by_folder when you need metadata (tags, type, related) along with paths. Prefer vault_search for content-based discovery. Use vault_read_note to read a note from the results.

Parameters:
- folder names a whole folder; without a glob, notes in its subfolders are listed too: "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/". Use the folder's exact letter case; on a case-sensitive filesystem a different case finds nothing.
- glob matches each note's path inside folder (its vault-relative path when folder is omitted), case-sensitively. * stays within one folder level and ** spans any depth: with folder "Projects", "**/*.md" lists every note under it.

Behavior: Paths come back sorted by vault-relative path in code-unit order (uppercase before lowercase). Hidden (dot-prefixed) notes and folders are never listed; symlinked notes are included.

Errors:
- A nonexistent folder or no glob matches returns an empty array, not an error.
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — use a vault-relative folder outside hidden folders, or omit folder to list the whole vault.
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …", "EACCES: …" or another filesystem error code — the message names the folder it could not read, and what to do; until then, pass a folder outside it.

Returns: JSON array of every matching vault-relative path, with no cap (e.g. ["Notes/idea.md", "Projects/plan.md"]).

tools.name: vault_list_property_keys
tools.title: List Property Keys
tools.description:
Discover all property keys in the vault with note counts and sample values. Lets you understand the vault's metadata schema without reading individual notes.

Example: vault_list_property_keys() returns [{ key: "tags", count: 342, sample_values: ["session-log", "project"] }, ...]
Example: vault_list_property_keys({ folder: "Projects" }) — the keys used under Projects/ only

When to use: Discovering what properties exist before searching by property. Good first step for vault orientation alongside vault_list_tags.
Prefer vault_list_property_values when you need the full list of values for a specific key. Prefer vault_search_by_property to find notes matching a specific key-value pair.

Parameters:
- folder names a whole folder and includes its subfolders: "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/". Matching ignores ASCII letter case; omit folder to scan the entire vault.

Behavior:
- Only frontmatter properties count; inline Dataview fields (key:: value) are not listed.
- count is the number of notes that have the key, including notes where its value is empty (null).
- sample_values are the key's 3 most frequent displayed strings, counting each array element separately; a checkbox appears as "1" or "0", and null values are skipped.

Errors:
- An empty vault or folder returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of { key, count, sample_values } sorted by count descending, then by key.

tools.name: vault_list_property_values
tools.title: List Property Values
tools.description:
List distinct values for a specific property key with how often each occurs.

Example: vault_list_property_values({ key: "status" }) returns [{ value: "done", count: 211 }, { value: "active", count: 47 }, ...]
Example: vault_list_property_values({ key: "tags", limit: 10 }) — the 10 most-used tags

When to use: Enumerating possible values for a property key before calling vault_search_by_property. Call vault_list_property_keys first to discover valid key names. vault_search_by_property matches stored numbers numerically and text exactly; value "1" matches the number 1, the text "1", and a checked checkbox.

Parameters:
- key is case-sensitive and must match exactly as returned by vault_list_property_keys.
- folder names a whole folder and includes its subfolders: "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/". Matching ignores ASCII letter case.
- limit applies after sorting by count descending, so you always get the most-used values first. Nothing in the response signals truncation: exactly limit values may mean more exist, which is common for keys with many distinct values like "title" or "created"; raise limit to check.

Behavior:
- Handles both scalar properties (status: "active") and array properties (tags: ["a", "b"]). Array elements are unpacked and counted individually, so the sum of counts may exceed the note count.
- Values with the same displayed string share one row with combined occurrence counts: number 1 and text "1" count together, while text "1.0" stays separate. Grouping happens before limit.
- Checkbox true and false come back as "1" and "0", counted with the numbers 1 and 0.
- null values are skipped.

Errors:
- An unknown key or empty folder returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of { value, count } sorted by count descending, then by value in binary text order ("10" before "2").

tools.name: vault_list_tags
tools.title: List Tags
tools.description:
List all tags in the vault with note counts, ordered by count descending, then by tag name. Only frontmatter tags Obsidian accepts are counted, not inline #tags. Spellings that differ only in letter case are one tag, shown as the spelling written most often. Each hierarchical tag appears as one full entry, not split into segments. Count is unique notes, not occurrences.

Example: vault_list_tags() returns [{ tag: "session-log", count: 42 }, { tag: "project/vault-cortex", count: 8 }, ...]

When to use: Discovering what tags exist before searching by tag. Good first step for vault orientation.
Prefer vault_search_by_tag once you know which tag to query — it supports hierarchical prefix matching ("project" matches "project/*"). To count tags in one folder, or only the most-used ones, use vault_list_property_values({ key: "tags" }) with folder or limit; it counts every value of the tags property and lists spellings that differ in letter case apart.

Errors:
- A vault with no tagged notes returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of { tag, count }; tag omits the "#" prefix.

tools.name: vault_list_tasks
tools.title: List Tasks
tools.description:
List checkbox tasks across the whole vault with structured filters — the Tasks-plugin data model over MCP. Both task metadata formats are indexed: emoji signifiers (📅 due, ⏳ scheduled, 🛫 start, ➕ created, ✅ done, ❌ cancelled, 🔺⏫🔼🔽⏬ priority, 🔁 recurrence, 🏁 onCompletion, 🆔/⛔ dependencies) and Dataview inline fields ([due:: 2026-07-04], [priority:: high], ...). Every result says where the task lives (see Returns), so no follow-up reads are needed to locate it. Task lines inside fenced code blocks and %% %% comment blocks are not indexed. Checkboxes typed NON_TASK in the Tasks plugin's status settings are also excluded.

Example: vault_list_tasks({ due: { before: "2026-07-04" } }) — overdue triage; the default status (not_done) and sort (due ascending) make this the "what's overdue?" call
Example: vault_list_tasks({ path: "Code Projects/vault-cortex/TASKS.md", heading: ["Active", "Up Next", "Waiting On"], sort_by: "position" }) — actionable Kanban lanes in board order
Example: vault_list_tasks({ folder: "Code Projects/vault-cortex" }) — all open tasks across a project tree (TASKS.md + task-notes/ subdirectories)
Example: vault_list_tasks({ status: "done", done: { after: "2026-06-26" } }) — what got completed this week
Example: vault_list_tasks({ top_level_only: true, path: "TASKS.md" }) — board cards only, excluding checklist sub-items

When to use: Reading task status and order on one board (path + sort_by: "position"; add status: "all" to include done and cancelled cards). Also any vault-wide task triage question — "what's overdue?", "what's open per project?", "what did I finish this week?" — in one call instead of per-board reads.
Prefer vault_read_note (heading mode) only when you need a lane's verbatim Markdown or a task's state right after a write. Prefer vault_search for full-text queries over note content.

Behavior: A file change takes a few seconds to appear here, so a task written moments ago may still show its old state.

Parameters:
- status: "not_done" and "all" expand in arrays — ["not_done", "done"] matches todo + in_progress + done.
- due / scheduled / start / done / created / cancelled: a date filter only matches tasks that HAVE that date.
- folder: a whole folder, subfolders included ("Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/"), ignoring ASCII letter case.
- sort_by: a task with none of a date sort's dates comes last; "priority" ascending puts highest first, and tasks with no priority sort between medium and low.

Errors:
- "invalid due.before date: …" (any date filter's bound) — the bound isn't in YYYY-MM-DD form; use that form
- "… is not a calendar date" — a date filter's bound has the YYYY-MM-DD form but names a day that doesn't exist, such as 2026-02-30; pass a real date
- "path must end in …" — add the ".md" extension
- "tag must not be empty …" — tag is "#" alone; pass the tag name
- No matches returns { total: 0, tasks: [] }, not an error
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON { total, tasks }. Every task carries path, line, status, status_char (the checkbox character, such as "x" or "/"), description, folder (the task note's parent folder, e.g. "Code Projects/vault-cortex"), depth (0 for top-level, 1+ for sub-tasks), is_kanban_task (true when the task's note is a Kanban board, with kanban-plugin in its properties), depends_on, and tags (the arrays are [] when empty). Every other field appears only when the task has it: heading (nearest heading above the task), created/scheduled/start/due/done/cancelled dates, priority, recurrence, on_completion, task_id, block_id, parent_block_id (sub-tasks whose parent carries a ^block-id), done_lanes (Kanban boards only: the headings of the lanes whose first line is **Complete**), and subtask_progress — { done, total } over the task's DIRECT checklist children, present only when the task has a checklist; done counts status "done" only (a cancelled child counts toward total, not done), and the counts ignore the query's filters — so a filtered or top_level_only read still shows each card's checklist progress.

status.description: Status filter, OR-combined (default "not_done" = todo + in_progress, excluding done and cancelled). "all" includes every status.

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

priority.description: Priority levels, OR-combined; "none" selects tasks with no priority signifier

tag.description: Tag on the task line, "#" optional; matches nested tags, any letter case

heading.description: Exact heading text or array of headings, OR-combined, case-sensitive (e.g. "Active" or ["Active", "Up Next"])

path.description: Restrict to one note (vault-relative path ending ".md", case-sensitive)

top_level_only.description: When true, only top-level tasks (depth 0) are returned — excludes indented sub-tasks and checklist items. Default false.

limit.description: Max results (default 50); total always reports the full match count

sort_by.description: Sort key (default "due"). Date sorts cascade through related fields when the primary is absent (through the rest of due → scheduled → start → created, in that order; done does not cascade). "position" sorts by file path then line number — the natural order for Kanban boards.

sort_direction.description: Sort direction. Default per field: "asc" for due/scheduled/priority/position, "desc" for start/created/done/note_mtime. When a date sort cascades (see sort_by), each field uses its own default direction; an explicit value overrides all fields uniformly.

tools.name: vault_memory_recall
tools.title: Memory Recall
tools.description:
Recall memory entries about a topic — entry-granular hybrid (keyword + semantic) retrieval across ALL About Me/ files and ALL time. Returns the relevant dated entries, up to limit, sorted oldest-first, so the full evolution of a preference, opinion, or fact is visible — semantic matching finds early entries even when their phrasing differs from the query. Tuned for recall over precision: expect some marginal entries and judge relevance yourself when synthesizing an answer. Content-word queries ("testing philosophy", "sustainable pacing") rank best. A meta-framed query ("opinions on testing") that scores below the relevance threshold degrades to relaxed any-term keyword matching instead of returning nothing.

Example: vault_memory_recall({ query: "working hours and pacing" })
Example: vault_memory_recall({ query: "testing philosophy", file: "Opinions" })

When to use: Answering "what does my memory say about X?" or "how has my view on Y evolved?" — topic-based recall across memory files. Prefer vault_get_memory to read a known file or section verbatim; prefer vault_search for notes outside the memory layer.

Behavior: A memory file change takes a few seconds to appear here, so an entry written moments ago may not be recalled yet.

Errors:
- No matching entries returns { entries: [], total: 0, truncated: false, search_mode, reranked }, not an error
- An unknown file returns empty results — call vault_list_memory_files to discover valid names
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON { entries, total, truncated, search_mode, reranked }. Each entry is { file, section, date, text } — text is the raw entry markdown (wikilinks intact, continuation lines included); file and section feed directly into vault_get_memory. The total counts every matched entry; truncated=true means limit dropped the least-relevant matches, whatever their dates, so raise limit or narrow the query for the complete set. The file filter is applied before limit, so limit keeps the most relevant matches from that file. The search_mode value is "hybrid" when vector matching contributed and "fts" when the entries came from keyword matching alone — including the any-term fallback; reranked is true when the reranker's relevance cut was applied.

query.description: Topic to recall, in natural language.

file.description: Optional: restrict to one memory file, name without .md (e.g. "Opinions"), in its exact letter case. Omit for cross-file recall — the default and usual choice.

tools.name: vault_read_note
tools.title: Read Note
tools.description:
Read a markdown note by its vault-relative path. By default returns the full raw content including properties; optional modes return just the properties, just the heading outline, or just one section.

Example: vault_read_note({ path: "Projects/vault-cortex.md" })
Example: vault_read_note({ path: "Projects/vault-cortex.md", properties_only: true })
Example: vault_read_note({ path: "TASKS.md", outline: true })
Example: vault_read_note({ path: "TASKS.md", heading: "Active" })
Example: vault_read_note({ path: "TASKS.md", heading: "Done", heading_level: 2 }) // disambiguate when several "Done" headings exist
Example: vault_read_note({ path: "TASKS.md", heading: "Done", start_line: 1, limit: 20 }) // first 20 lines of an oversized section

When to use: You know the exact path and need a specific note's content. For a large note (a long Kanban board or doc), use outline: true to see its headings and any text sitting above them, then heading: "..." to read just the one section you need. For a note or section too long for one response (this tool sets no cap; the outline gives each section's bytes), page it with start_line and limit to read a window at a time. To check a note's or section's line count, request start_line: 1 with limit: 1 — one line plus the total.
Prefer vault_search when you don't know the path. For task status or order on a board, prefer vault_list_tasks; heading mode returns a lane's Markdown. Prefer vault_get_memory for About Me/ files (returns content without properties). To explore what links to this note or what it links to, use vault_get_backlinks and vault_get_outgoing_links.

Section boundaries: a section spans from its heading to the next heading of the same or higher level (or EOF). Child headings are included.

Errors:
- "note not found" — no note exists at this path; verify it with vault_list_notes
- "heading not found" — the message lists the available headings
- "ambiguous heading" — multiple headings match; use heading_level to disambiguate, or read the full note (omit heading) when headings share the same level
- "outline, heading, and properties_only are mutually exclusive — set at most one"
- "heading_level requires a heading" — pass heading with it
- "heading cannot be empty" — heading is whitespace only; pass the heading's text
- "line paging is not available in outline mode" / "… properties_only mode" — start_line and limit page only a full read or a heading section
- "start line past the end" — the message states the line count; resend a start_line within it
- 'path must end in ".md"' — add the extension to a note's path
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — use a vault-relative path with no hidden (dot-prefixed) file or folder in it
- "properties block is not valid YAML …" — a full read, outline and heading still work; the error says how to repair it
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …", "EACCES: …" or another filesystem error code — the message says what to do

Returns: Raw markdown string (default); JSON object of properties, {} when the note has none (properties_only); JSON outline object, shaped as the outline parameter describes (outline); raw markdown of the section, heading line included (heading). When start_line or limit is given, the result is preceded by a window-metadata text block ("path — lines 1–20 of 250 (continue with start_line: 21)"). Unpaged full reads return the file's exact bytes; heading sections and paged reads use LF line endings.

Outline: bytes at the root is the whole file's on-disk size and modified is its filesystem modification time (ISO 8601); each heading's bytes is the exact UTF-8 byte length of the text that heading mode returns for that section. Empty headings ("##" with no text) appear with text: "" — they act as section boundaries but cannot be targeted by the heading parameter; read the parent section or the full note.

path.description: Vault-relative path to the note, including the ".md" extension (e.g. "About Me/Principles.md"). Use the exact letter case.

properties_only.description: If true, returns parsed properties as JSON instead of full note content

outline.description: If true, returns { bytes, modified, leading_callout?, leading_content?, headings } as JSON instead of body content. headings: [{ level, text, bytes }]; leading_callout: { type, title, body } when the note has a top-of-file callout; leading_content: the rest of the body text above the first heading (callout lines excluded) when the note has any.

heading.description: Return only this section. Case-sensitive exact match.

heading_level.description: Heading level (1-6) for disambiguation when multiple headings share the same text

tools.name: vault_recent_notes
tools.title: Recent Notes
tools.description:
List recently modified or created notes, sorted by timestamp — a time-ordered window into the vault, not a date-range filter.

Example: vault_recent_notes({ sort_by: "modified", limit: 10 })
Example: vault_recent_notes({ sort_by: "created", limit: 5 })

When to use: Catching up on vault changes, finding recent work, or orienting after a break.
Prefer vault_search for content-based discovery, including a text query limited to a date range (its created and modified filters). Prefer vault_search_by_folder for browsing a specific folder.

Parameters:
- sort_by + limit interact: "modified" uses filesystem mtime, which every note has. "created" uses the frontmatter created property; notes without a valid one sort after every dated note, so a small limit can leave them out — use "modified" to see them.
- sort_by "modified" includes any file write (content edits, property changes, sync touches), so recently-synced notes appear recent even without user edits.

Behavior: A file change takes a few seconds to appear here, so a note written moments ago may not be listed yet.

Errors:
- An empty vault returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of note metadata (path, title, tags, related, folder (top-level folder), type, created, modified, bytes, leading_callout, additional_properties), newest first. The created field is null when the property is missing or not an ISO date; bytes is on-disk file size. A leading_callout field appears only when the note has one; additional_properties only when frontmatter has keys outside title, type, created, related, and tags.

sort_by.description: Timestamp to sort by, newest first (default "modified")

tools.name: vault_search
tools.title: Search Notes
tools.description:
Hybrid search across vault notes, ranked by combined keyword and semantic relevance. Semantic matching finds notes even when exact keywords differ — "career aspirations" finds notes about "goals" and "targets". Unquoted terms use implicit AND with stemming ("running" also matches "run"); wrap in double quotes for exact phrases; punctuated terms (vault-cortex, deploy/local) are matched as exact adjacent-word phrases automatically.

Filters — all conditions AND-combine with each other and the text query:
- folder: a whole folder, subfolders included — "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/"; ignores ASCII letter case
- tags: every listed frontmatter tag must match, in any letter case; "project" also matches "project/a"
- properties: keys and text values match exactly, letter case included; values compare by exact type — pass a number as a number, not "4". Exception: true and false compare as 1 and 0, so true or 1 matches a checked checkbox and the number 1. A list property matches when any element equals the value.
- created / modified: bounds compare whole calendar days in the server's time zone (returned created and modified values show its UTC offset), so "on" matches anywhere within the day. Notes without a parseable created property never match a created filter

Example: vault_search({ query: "how the server watches for file changes" })
Example: vault_search({ query: "kubernetes networking", filters: { tags: ["reference"] } })
Example: vault_search({ query: "meeting notes", filters: { type: "meeting", folder: "Work" } })
Example: vault_search({ query: "decision", filters: { modified: { after: "2026-06-30" } } }) — matching notes touched in July or later

When to use: The primary discovery tool for content-based queries, optionally constrained by metadata. Try natural-language queries, not just keywords.
Prefer vault_search_by_tag for tag-only queries without text. Prefer vault_search_by_folder for browsing a folder. Prefer vault_search_by_property for metadata-only queries. Prefer vault_recent_notes for time-based browsing.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds, so a note written moments ago may not be found yet.

Errors:
- No matches returns { results: [], total: 0, search_mode, reranked }, not an error
- Malformed query syntax never throws: the words AND, OR, NOT and NEAR in any letter case, and punctuation such as *, ^, parentheses and colons, are dropped before keyword matching; a query left with no terms is matched by meaning only, or finds nothing when only keyword matching ran (search_mode "fts")
- "invalid created.on date: …" (any created/modified bound) — the bound isn't in YYYY-MM-DD form; use that form
- "… is not a calendar date" — a created/modified bound has the YYYY-MM-DD form but names a day that doesn't exist, such as 2026-02-30; pass a real date
- "tag must not be empty …" — a tags entry is only "#"; pass the tag name
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON with results array (path, title, snippet, score, tags, folder (top-level folder), type, kind, created, modified, bytes), total (results returned, not all matches; a total equal to limit may mean more exist, so raise limit to check), search_mode ("hybrid" when vector embeddings contributed, "fts" when only keyword matching ran), and reranked (true when reranking refined the ordering). A higher score is more relevant. The kind field is always "note". The created field is omitted, not null, when a result has none; type is null when the result has no type property. The bytes field is the on-disk file size. With include_leading_callout, each result also carries leading_callout ({ type, title, body }) when present.

related.description: Require all listed related links, each written exactly as in the note's related property, brackets and alias included (e.g. "[[Projects/alpha|Alpha]]")

type.description: Match the frontmatter type field (exact, case-sensitive match, e.g. "person", "meeting")

properties.description: Match arbitrary frontmatter properties by key-value (e.g. { status: "active", priority: 1 })

created.description: Created date bounds (YYYY-MM-DD) on the frontmatter "created" property

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

modified.description: Modified date bounds (YYYY-MM-DD) on filesystem modified time

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

snippet_tokens.description: Snippet length in words, not model tokens (default 30)

include_leading_callout.description: If true, include each result's leading callout.

tools.name: vault_search_by_folder
tools.title: Search by Folder
tools.description:
Browse notes in a folder with full metadata.

Example: vault_search_by_folder({ folder: "Projects" })
Example: vault_search_by_folder({ folder: "About Me", recursive: false, limit: 10 }) — the folder's own notes, 10 most recent

When to use: Exploring a folder's contents with full context for vault orientation.
Prefer vault_list_notes when you only need paths. Prefer vault_search when you have a text query. Use vault_get_backlinks or vault_get_outgoing_links to explore how notes in a folder connect to the rest of the vault.

Parameters:
- folder names a whole folder, not a text prefix: "Projects" matches notes under "Projects/" but not "ProjectsOld/". Matching ignores ASCII letter case, and a trailing slash is ignored.
- limit applies after sorting, so you get the most recently modified notes. There is no offset, and nothing in the response signals truncation: exactly limit results may mean more exist, so raise limit to see them.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds: a note written moments ago may not appear yet, one renamed or deleted moments ago may still be listed, and a just-changed note may show its old metadata. Notes in hidden (dot-prefixed) folders never appear.

Errors:
- An empty or nonexistent folder returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of note metadata sorted by most recently modified, then by path: path, title (file name without .md when missing or not text), tags, related ([] when missing), folder (top-level folder), type (null when missing or not text), created (frontmatter; null when missing or not an ISO date), modified (file time), bytes (on-disk size), plus, when present, leading_callout (the note's opening callout, { type, title, body }) and additional_properties (other frontmatter keys).

recursive.description: Include subfolders (default: true); false lists only the folder's top level

tools.name: vault_search_by_property
tools.title: Search by Property
tools.description:
Find notes where a frontmatter property matches a value.

Example: vault_search_by_property({ key: "status", value: "in-progress" })
Example: vault_search_by_property({ key: "type", value: "session-log", folder: "Code Projects" })

When to use: Finding notes by metadata when you don't have a text query.
Prefer vault_search when you also have a text query (it supports property filters too). Prefer vault_search_by_tag for tag-specific queries (supports hierarchical prefix matching). Use vault_list_property_keys to discover valid keys and vault_list_property_values to see what values a key takes.

Parameters:
- key matches exactly and case-sensitively; value matches stored text the same way, with no partial matching or globbing.
- A value written as a complete, finite YAML number (-4, 04, .5, 4., 1e3, 0x1F, 0o17) also matches stored numbers numerically: "04" and "4.0" match number 4 and their own literal text, but not text "4". Anything else ("4abc", " 4", 0b binary, "1e999") matches only as text. Numbers compare as 64-bit floats, so integers past 2^53 can compare equal and "1e-999" matches 0.
- value for a checkbox: pass "1" (checked) or "0" (unchecked); a checkbox matches only as text, so "1.0" and "true" do not match.
- value against a list property: an element must equal value in full: "blog" matches tags: ["blog", "draft"] but not tags: ["my-blog"].
- folder names a whole folder and includes its subfolders: "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/". Matching ignores ASCII letter case; omit folder to search the entire vault.
- limit keeps the most recently modified matches. Nothing in the response signals truncation: exactly limit results may mean more exist, so raise limit to check.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds: a note written moments ago may not match yet, and one changed moments ago may still match its old value.

Errors:
- An unknown key or unmatched value returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of note metadata (path, title, tags, related, folder, type, created, modified, bytes, leading_callout?, additional_properties?), sorted by filesystem mtime descending, then by path — recently-synced notes may sort ahead of older content edits.
- folder is the top-level folder ("" at the vault root); title falls back to the file name without .md when missing or not text; related is [] when missing; type is null when missing or not text; created is null when missing or not an ISO date.
- leading_callout appears only when the note has a leading callout.
- additional_properties appears only when frontmatter has keys outside title, type, created, related, and the first key spelled tags in any letter case.

tools.name: vault_search_by_tag
tools.title: Search by Tag
tools.description:
Find notes by frontmatter tag, ignoring letter case; inline #tags in note bodies are not searched. Unless exact is true, a tag also matches every tag nested under it at any depth: "project" matches "project/vault-cortex" and "project/a/b". A nested tag continues with "/", so "project" never matches "projects" or "my-project".

Example: vault_search_by_tag({ tag: "project" })
Example: vault_search_by_tag({ tag: "project", exact: true, limit: 50 }) — notes tagged "project" itself, up to 50

When to use: Tag-only lookups, for one tag or a whole tag hierarchy, with no text query. Use vault_list_tags first to discover available tags.
Prefer vault_search when you need text-based relevance ranking.

Parameters:
- limit applies after sorting, so you get the most recently modified notes. Nothing in the response signals truncation: a result count equal to limit may mean more exist, so raise limit to check.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds: a note written moments ago may not appear yet, and one moved, deleted, or retagged moments ago may still be listed.

Errors:
- An unknown tag or no matches returns an empty array, not an error.
- "project/" matches neither "project" nor "project/a"; drop the "/".
- "tag must not be empty …" — tag is "#" alone; pass the tag name.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of notes sorted by most recently modified, then by path ascending. Each note has path, folder (top-level folder; "" at the vault root), bytes (on-disk size), modified (file modification time), and the frontmatter values title (file name without .md when missing or not text), tags (every frontmatter tag Obsidian accepts, in the note's letter case), related ([] when missing), type (null when missing or not text), and created (null when missing or not an ISO date). Timestamps are ISO 8601. When present, a note also has leading_callout (the callout opening its body, as { type, title, body }) and additional_properties (every other frontmatter key).

exact.description: Match only the tag itself (default: false)

prompts.title: Daily review & reconciliation
prompts.description: Reconcile a day — daily note, vault-wide task status (due/overdue, scheduled), modified notes, and links — surface what happened, what's open, and durable facts worth saving to About Me/ memory.

arguments.name: date
arguments.description: Day to review in YYYY-MM-DD format (defaults to today)

arguments.name: max_chars
arguments.description: Optional cap on embedded content length (characters); omit for full content
